notes:
Summary: mid-market product analytics SaaS (B2B). Started on Hosted API for fast experiments in Q4 2025; now moving to Dedicated for predictable latency and cost at scale. Primary contact: CTO - Maya Singh; Procurement lead: Ben Carter. AE/SE: Ava Patel / Diego Morales. CSM tentatively assigned for onboarding: Natalie Brooks.

Timeline & activity (bulletized, CRM style):
- 2025-11-15: Intro call (Ava) — quick demo of chat + embeddings; interested in reducing 3rd-party token costs.
- 2025-12-02: Hosted API POC kickoff — integrated embeddings for product search; stable results.
- 2026-01-28: Feature demo + perf baseline (Fireflies: ffx_20260128_0102-signharbor-demo) — measured p95 latency = 220ms on hosted for typical 64-token prompts.
- 2026-02-12: Internal infra review, asked about VPC/private control plane options.
- 2026-02-22: Pricing call with engineering + procurement (Fireflies: ffx_20260222_0915-pricing-call) — asked for commit/burst examples and ramp schedule.

POC & technical notes:
- Workload: real-time support assistant + semantic search for product docs; heavy embedding index updates during off-peak.
- Targets: p95 latency <150ms for chat; steady-state throughput ~40-60 QPS (burstable to 90 QPS).
- Running latest open model variants; experimenting with int8 quantized variants for cost.
- KV cache and prefix caching will be critical to hit latency SLOs. SE suggested dedicated GPU pool + 2x KV cache nodes.

Pricing/packaging negotiation summary (current state):
- Customer wants a 12–24 month committed Dedicated contract. Key asks: low committed baseline with predictable overage band, documented burst window, and month-by-month ramp schedule.
- Proposed Redwood structure discussed: commit tiers (50k tokens/day, 150k tokens/day, 300k tokens/day equivalence), burst allowance = +30% sustained for short windows, overage rate = 1.5x unit rate above committed baseline.
- Signal Harbor pushed back: wants burst to be larger for quarterly product launches (asking for burst up to +60% for 72-hour windows) and a grace overage tier for first 90 days of ramp.
- Agreed compromise in call: 30% standard burst, optional 72-hr manual burst at negotiated uplift with pre-authorized credit card hold or PO amendment. Grace ramp: month1 = 30% of committed, month2 = 60%, month3 = 100% (agreed in principle, needs SOW).
- Discount structure: tiered ARR discounts at 12/18/24 month terms; early-pay incentive (net-30 -> additional 2% credit).
- Outstanding pricing points: exact overage multiplier for large bursts, definition of "sustained" for burst windows, invoice cadence and metric reporting granularity.

Security & compliance items:
- Must support SSO/SAML, integrate with customer KMS, provide audit logs and retention controls. Data residency for EU customers flagged but not required now.
- Security questionnaire (Drive link above) has 6 open items — priority to close before legal routing.

Quotes & direct customer language:
- CTO Maya Singh: "We need predictable unit economics — surprises on token spend are a deal breaker."
- Procurement Ben Carter: "If we get a clear burst policy and a reasonable ramp, we can greenlight a 12-month commit."

Next steps (short):

- Legal to review MSA redlines (customer sent edits 2026-03-02).
- SE to deliver final perf projection with dedicated config (Diego) by 2026-03-10.
- Procurement to confirm internal budget band by 2026-03-17.
